$comment: Showroom product catalogue. `repo` is relative to the repo root and is only read by scripts/sync-content.ts (never at runtime). Live URLs may be overridden per deployment with the listed env vars. `capabilities`, `availableNow` and `roadmap` are curated for the public product pages: `availableNow` tracks the MVP scope in the workspace PLAN.md §4 and `roadmap` tracks each product's own docs/architecture/limits.md — re-check both after a content sync. `outcomes` is the customer-facing 'what you get' band on the public product page, used until the marketing lead supplies a `customer.outcomes` block in content/site/<product>.json.

products.summary: Turn PDFs, scans and photographed forms into validated, structured records through one API call.

capabilities.title: One call in, a canonical record out
capabilities.body: POST a PDF, an image of a form or a scanned statement and get back typed fields with confidence scores, named entities, a summary and validation issues.

capabilities.title: Eleven built-in document types
capabilities.body: Invoices, claims, contracts, statements, purchase orders and more ship as schemas; anything else is a custom extraction config away.

capabilities.title: Watch the pipeline run
capabilities.body: Every upload becomes a job with a live event stream: process, classify, extract, entities, summarise, validate, standardise.

capabilities.title: Export or interrogate
capabilities.body: Export a record as JSON, XML or CSV, or ask the document a question and get a grounded, cited answer.

availableNow: Versioned `/api/v1` with an OpenAPI 3.1 contract, Redoc and Swagger UI
Upload by multipart or raw body, with asynchronous jobs and SSE progress events
Eleven built-in schemas plus custom extraction configurations provisioned into ARAG
Exports in JSON, XML and CSV, plus grounded question answering over a single document
Admin panel: configuration, Knowledge Box connection test, usage, jobs and logs
roadmap: Multi-tenant isolation — the MVP is a single Knowledge Box with one service account
Bulk/batch upload and a review queue for low-confidence fields
Scheduled retention purges (today the TTL cleanup is an admin action)
A wider set of built-in document types and locale-specific validation rules

outcomes.title: Fewer hours spent keying data
outcomes.body: Documents that arrive as pictures of data — PDFs, photographed forms, scanned statements — come back as typed fields your systems can read, without anyone retyping them.

outcomes.title: Know which fields to check
outcomes.body: Every field carries a confidence score and the original raw value, and arithmetic that does not reconcile is flagged as an explicit issue rather than passed through as a silent guess.

outcomes.title: A new document layout is not a project
outcomes.body: There are no per-vendor templates to tune. Eleven common document types are built in, and anything else is a schema you describe once.

outcomes.title: Data that lands where you need it
outcomes.body: Export the same record as JSON, XML or CSV, or ask the document a direct question and get an answer grounded in its own text.

products.summary: Every recorded contact-centre call becomes a labeled, searchable, citable record — with no analyst tagging a single call by hand.

capabilities.title: Automatic labelling, no analyst tagging
capabilities.body: Call reason, outcome, sentiment, line of business and disposition flags are applied by data-augmentation agents the moment a recording lands.

capabilities.title: Moments inside the transcript
capabilities.body: Individual paragraphs are labelled too — compliance disclosure, escalation, cross-sell — so a reviewer can scrub straight to the moment that matters.

capabilities.title: Ask one call a question
capabilities.body: The chat is scoped to a single call's transcript, and every citation clicks through to the exact paragraph and scrubs the recording to it.

capabilities.title: A dashboard over the whole queue
capabilities.body: Volumes, sentiment, complaint and cross-sell rates, and agent scorecards aggregated from structured fields rather than sampled by hand.

availableNow: Versioned `/api/v1` with an OpenAPI 3.1 contract, Redoc and Swagger UI
Call list with search and facets, per-call detail with a synchronised transcript and player
Grounded per-call question answering with clickable, timestamped citations
Queue-wide dashboard aggregated from the agents' structured output
Admin panel: agent/task status, idempotent provisioning, cache inspection, health and logs
roadmap: Real-time and in-call use — the MVP analyses a call after it has been recorded
Per-user authorisation; today any holder of a valid key can read every call in the Knowledge Box
Multi-tenant deployment across more than one Knowledge Box
Coaching workflows built on the scorecard output

outcomes.title: Every call reviewed, not a 2% sample
outcomes.body: Each recording is transcribed, classified and scored the moment it lands, so quality assurance stops being a sampling exercise.

outcomes.title: Jump straight to the moment
outcomes.body: Individual passages are labelled too, so a reviewer clicks a moment — a disclosure, an escalation, a complaint — and the recording scrubs to that second.

outcomes.title: Ask a call a question
outcomes.body: Answers come only from that call's own transcript, and every citation clicks through to the exact passage it came from.

outcomes.title: See the whole queue at once
outcomes.body: Volumes, sentiment, complaint and resolution rates aggregate from structured fields rather than from what anyone had time to listen to.

products.summary: The discipline layer between a voice agent and a Knowledge Box: every spoken answer grounded, cited, or handed to a human by rule.

capabilities.title: Real-time listening
capabilities.body: Feed a live conversation transcript in and a grounded, cited brief streams back as the call evolves — topic, goal, stage, suggested questions and answers.

capabilities.title: Handoff by rule, not by vibe
capabilities.body: When retrieval does not cover the question the caller hears the configured handoff line. The check is deterministic, not a judgement the model makes about itself.

capabilities.title: Nothing spoken that should not be
capabilities.body: Citations are structured data shown on screen; URLs, markdown and citation markers are stripped from anything destined for speech.

capabilities.title: Provable before it goes live
capabilities.body: A golden-question corpus gates a prospect's configuration: the demo does not open until the grounding and handoff checks pass.

availableNow: Versioned `/api/v1` with an OpenAPI 3.1 contract, Redoc and Swagger UI
Headless listen sessions: transcript chunk ingestion and an SSE stream of evolving briefs
Grounded voice answers with deterministic handoff and structured citations
Prospect registry with stored ARAG search configurations and per-prospect health checks
Golden-evaluation runs, turn-log inspection and metrics in the admin panel
roadmap: Self-serve voice deflection as the follow-on to agent-assist
Per-agent authentication on the core answer endpoint (today it is one shared service token)
Production-grade safety guards; the MVP's input/output guards are demo-grade
A verified LiveAvatar integration and a durable store to replace the single-writer JSON files

outcomes.title: The right answer, while the call is still happening
outcomes.body: A live conversation streams in and an evolving, cited brief keeps up: who the other person is, what they want, and what to say next.

outcomes.title: Never the wrong answer, confidently
outcomes.body: When your own content does not cover the question, the system hands off by a deterministic rule instead of guessing — and the rule is testable.

outcomes.title: Evidence on screen, not in the ear
outcomes.body: Citations are structured data your team can see and check; nothing spoken ever contains a URL or a citation marker.

outcomes.title: Proved before it goes live
outcomes.body: A fixed set of questions it must answer and questions it must refuse runs through the real pipeline before anyone trusts it.
